title: MetaInfer → VibeQwen: from construction workflow to serving stack
summary: An author-reported experiment adapted MetaInfer and reused existing kernels to build a deployment-specific Qwen serving stack.
summary_cn: 一个改造智能体工作流、复用现有内核来构建专用执行栈的实验案例。
motivation: Target lower latency than a general engine for Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 on one B200.
boundary: Model execution and serving integration, evaluated as deployed services; public VibeQwen engine source was not established.
reuse: vLLM/TensorRT-LLM kernels and references; MetaInfer is the adapted workflow, not VibeQwen source.
tradeoff: NVFP4 numerical differences were accepted if accuracy against BF16 was at least as good.
construction: Agent build/deploy/profile iterations: about one week, 1.7B mostly cached tokens and approximately 200 B200-hours.
ai_role: Disclosed: Claude Code with human steering, deployment access and measurement tools.
cost: Resource usage reported; fee estimates do not establish total development cost.
validation: Author-reported performance and accuracy checks; experimental, not production. No independent reproduction here.
maintenance: Long-term compatibility, regression coverage and maintenance effort were not established by the report.

title: Sol-Engine: compose and qualify model-specific optimizations
summary: An agent-oriented workflow assembles model-specific video execution paths from reusable optimizations and measured quality constraints.
summary_cn: 以智能体工作流组合模型专用优化，并以延迟和图像质量约束筛选配置。
motivation: The README identifies denoising-step redundancy, sparse interactions and repeated memory-bound operations as optimization opportunities.
boundary: The reviewed artifact is an optimized video codebase and configuration workflow, not a replacement for every serving layer.
reuse: Builds on SGLang multimodal_gen and existing model pipelines; combines cache, quantization, fusion, sparse attention and pruning.
tradeoff: Cache, sparsity and precision choices can change outputs; their effects must be separated from exact implementation changes.
construction: Documented workflow: executors explore configurations; an orchestrator checks, deduplicates and integrates results into reproducible run bundles.
ai_role: Intrinsic: the documented onboarding and optimization workflow uses coding agents; authored kernels remain reusable components.
cost: Total development tokens, GPU-hours and human maintenance costs are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: Documented gates include LPIPS, visual review and checks that optimizations actually engaged; these are not equivalence proofs.
maintenance: Per-model hooks and backend combinations need qualification; long-term maintenance effort is not established.

title: Flash-MoE: SSD-streamed experts in a native prototype
summary: A fixed-model C/Metal prototype streams expert weights from SSD and controls the execution pipeline directly.
summary_cn: 围绕固定模型和苹果统一内存机器，直接组织 SSD 专家读取与 C/Metal 执行。
motivation: The stated target is running Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on a 48 GB MacBook despite weights exceeding RAM.
boundary: Owns model inference, routing, I/O and Metal execution; this is a narrow research prototype rather than a generic loader.
reuse: Uses Apple Metal, Accelerate BLAS, dispatch groups and the operating-system page cache alongside pretrained model weights.
tradeoff: The executable uses four experts although its source identifies ten active experts in the model; quantization adds another change.
construction: The author reports human–AI prototype construction; C/Metal sources expose the result. Detailed task division and iteration history are not established.
ai_role: Disclosed: the project describes a human-and-AI build. That statement does not establish autonomous correctness.
cost: The README reports a 24-hour human–AI prototype build; total lifecycle expenditure is not disclosed.
validation: The K=4 source and reported 2-bit JSON failures prevent treating headline speed as an equivalent top-10 baseline.
maintenance: Model geometry and packed files are specific; broader compatibility and sustained maintenance are not established.

title: DwarfStar: a deliberately narrow native execution stack
summary: A native stack integrates selected model paths, state management and local serving around consumer-hardware constraints.
summary_cn: 以少数模型和消费级硬件为边界，联合构建原生执行、状态管理与本地服务。
motivation: The author explicitly cites capable local models, expert quantization, compressed KV and fast SSDs as reasons for specialization.
boundary: Owns a narrow inference path plus CLI/server integration; it deliberately does not accept arbitrary GGUF models.
reuse: Its ds4.c inference path does not link GGML, but credits llama.cpp/GGML and retains or adapts quantization layouts, CPU logic and kernels.
tradeoff: Capacity depends on resident state, expert precision and SSD traffic; model coverage is intentionally selective.
construction: Public artifacts show native model paths and adapted lower-level code; the author describes humans guiding agent-assisted implementation, testing and debugging.
ai_role: Disclosed: strong coding-agent assistance, with humans leading ideas, testing and debugging.
cost: Total construction time, token usage and engineering expenditure are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: The repository describes release QA and integrated tests; this survey did not reproduce its performance or numerical results.
maintenance: The author calls it beta and rapidly changing; supported models may be replaced as the project evolves.

title: Strata: tier experts around a gaming PC
summary: A Qwen-specific runtime combines GPU-resident work with CPU expert execution and explicit memory budgets.
summary_cn: 针对普通游戏电脑，将 GPU 热专家、CPU 冷专家和状态存储组合成模型专用运行时。
motivation: The stated goal is local Qwen3.8-Flash-Next inference on consumer NVIDIA or AMD PCs rather than server-sized GPU memory.
boundary: Integrates inference, memory policy and local APIs around one model family and qualified quantized layouts.
reuse: Credits GGML quantization formats, GPU dot/dequantization code, CPU expert kernels and the mtmd vision helper.
tradeoff: Eligible configurations enable route-tail-skip by default, dropping some missed experts; residency and CPU/GPU rounding also affect outputs.
construction: Public artifacts show a C++ runtime with CUDA/HIP and GGML-derived components. Development tools, task division and iteration history are not disclosed.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources. Compatibility with coding-agent clients is not evidence of AI-authored implementation.
cost: Development time, token expenditure and controlled construction-cost comparisons are not disclosed.
validation: Documented benchmark scenarios and source inspection expose configuration differences; no independent performance or quality reproduction was run.
maintenance: Device, quantization and skip-policy combinations require version-specific checks; maintenance effort is not disclosed.

title: NInfer: a native Qwen stack for one GPU
summary: Owns model execution, state and serving within a deliberately narrow checkpoint and GPU contract.
summary_cn: 围绕选定 Qwen 模型和 RTX 5090，自行组织模型计算、状态管理与请求服务。
motivation: The stated objective is maximum single-GPU performance for selected checkpoints; general model and device coverage is outside that target.
boundary: Native operators, model programs, state/KV management, scheduling and CLI/HTTP serving form one execution stack.
reuse: Retains pretrained weights, CUDA runtime, FFmpeg and HTTP/JSON/logging dependencies; owning execution does not imply a dependency-free system.
tradeoff: The upstream target is Linux with sm_120a, one resident model and startup-fixed execution lanes; it is not a general multi-device deployment contract.
construction: Public C++/CUDA modules and development contracts expose how components fit together. The actual development chronology and human–AI division of work are not disclosed.
ai_role: Not established. AI-assistance contribution policies and agent instruction files are not implementation-authorship evidence.
cost: Development effort and lifecycle costs are not disclosed; inference throughput does not establish construction economics.
validation: Published tests include independent operator oracles and opt-in real-engine integration checks. This survey did not execute them or reproduce performance.
maintenance: Explicit architecture and contribution boundaries constrain changes; artifact-version migration is documented, but sustained adaptation cost is unknown.

title: Splash: model-specific execution with agent-generated kernels
summary: Integrates a matched draft, specialized kernels and memory policy into a local Apple-silicon serving stack.
summary_cn: 围绕选定模型和 Apple 芯片，把专用草稿、内核与内存策略整合为本地执行栈，并披露由智能体生成专用内核。
motivation: The stated aim is efficient local model serving by specializing model dimensions, speculative execution and memory planning rather than maximizing model coverage.
boundary: C++/Metal code owns target/draft execution, kernels, scheduling and state management; a Python frontend exposes compatible HTTP APIs and vision input.
reuse: Uses existing checkpoints and tokenizers, Apple runtimes, and acknowledged llama.cpp-derived quantization tables and GGUF decoding material.
tradeoff: Targets selected Qwen families and compatible Bonsai checkpoints on recent Apple silicon. Quantized weights, KV precision and optional Neural Engine prefill affect comparison conditions.
construction: Public native modules expose integration; the official launch account describes internal agents creating and tuning kernels for model shapes, with precompiled variants shipped to users.
ai_role: Directly disclosed for specialized kernels. The record does not establish agent authorship of the scheduler, frontend or entire engine.
cost: No development-effort or total lifecycle-cost accounting was found; throughput measurements do not establish cheaper construction.
validation: Upstream provides numerical oracles, Metal tests, real-model checks and author-reported HTTP benchmarks. This survey inspected sources without running them.
maintenance: Architecture checks, pinned model revisions and documented release regressions support evolution; continuing model-porting effort and long-term maintenance cost remain unknown.

title: llamAmpere: specialize a shared runtime for Ampere and Qwen
summary: A deep llama.cpp fork integrates MTP verification, compressed KV state and SM86 execution for local long-context Qwen inference.
summary_cn: 深度改造 llama.cpp，将 MTP 验证、压缩 KV 和 SM86 执行路径整合为面向本地长上下文 Qwen 推理的系统。
motivation: Fit long-context Qwen3.8-27B inference on consumer Ampere GPUs while improving speculative verification and decode efficiency.
boundary: A substantial llama.cpp/TurboQuant fork changes kernels, speculative execution and state management; it is not a runtime built from scratch.
reuse: Retains GGML/GGUF, llama.cpp server and model infrastructure; extends TurboQuant/MTP paths and adapts KVarN-derived cache compression.
tradeoff: Optimized coverage centers on SM86/Qwen paths. Quantized KV and the recommended post-trained Swift derivative are not equivalent to original BF16 Qwen.
construction: Release articles trace profiling, candidate kernels, runtime fixes and rejected experiments; repeated upstream merges preserve shared capabilities and require integration repairs.
ai_role: Coding-agent contribution is not established. Handover notes mention Claude/Hermes sessions but do not attribute implementation or quantify task division.
cost: Development effort, agent expenditure and total maintenance cost are not disclosed in the reviewed sources.
validation: Authors report matched-setting speed tests and numerical checks; separate engine changes from checkpoint, KV format and sampling effects. Not independently reproduced here.
maintenance: Version 0.5.3 fixes cache-restoration and Blackwell build regressions; an unresolved parallel-8 failure limits extrapolation from single-stream results.

title: Gufo: a vertical runtime for Strix Halo
summary: A native C++/HIP engine chooses a narrow hardware target and selected models, owning execution, state and serving while adapting existing components.
summary_cn: 围绕 Strix Halo 和选定模型重建原生 C++/HIP 执行、状态管理与服务，并复用已有组件。
motivation: Focus on selected models that fit Strix Halo unified memory, concentrating optimization and testing instead of maximizing hardware and model coverage.
boundary: Owns model execution, kernels, sessions and local serving. Text/vision, ASR/TTS, image generation and video paths have different qualification levels.
reuse: Links ROCm/HIP and BLAS libraries; adapts llama.cpp/ggml quantized kernels, DS4 components and other attributed model code.
tradeoff: Production is restricted to Linux x86-64 gfx1151; supported checkpoints, quantization and speculative modes impose model-specific compatibility and quality limits.
construction: The documented development loop isolates each model’s C++/HIP library, kernels and reference checks. Historical implementation effort and human–AI task division are not disclosed.
ai_role: Not established: reviewed sources do not directly disclose AI authorship or task division; agent instructions do not establish either.
cost: Total development effort, human hours, agent tokens and long-term maintenance expenditure are not disclosed in the reviewed material.
validation: Author reports numerical and serving checks. Flash-Next vision fails one threshold; image coverage is small and full-video perceptual quality remains unqualified.
maintenance: Model-owned tests and quality records expose regression boundaries. Hosted CI covers CPU/repository checks; GPU qualification remains separate. No independent reproduction here.

title: Iris: own the image pipeline in C
summary: A C image-generation pipeline replaces framework-level execution for selected architectures while retaining platform acceleration.
summary_cn: 用 C 接管选定图像模型的完整推理流程，同时复用系统数学库和 GPU 能力。
motivation: The README emphasizes minimal runtime dependencies and memory-mapped execution on machines with limited RAM.
boundary: Implements text encoding, diffusion-transformer execution and image decoding for selected FLUX and Z-Image variants.
reuse: Consumes existing model weights and safetensors; accelerated paths use system Metal/MPS and optional BLAS.
tradeoff: Native implementation narrows dependencies, but CPU fallbacks and different model variants do not have identical performance or quality.
construction: Public artifacts show architecture-specific C implementation and platform backends. Sources describe C/Python reference debugging, but not the full development sequence or task division.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; disclosure from the author’s other projects must not be transferred to Iris.
cost: Construction time, AI-token spending and maintenance economics are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: The repository describes reference-image checks and C/Python debugging comparisons; performance and output claims were not independently reproduced.
maintenance: New architectures need implementation and reference checks; the reviewed sources do not quantify that continuing effort.

title: TensorFold: qualify native paths by checkpoint and platform
summary: A Zig server admits explicit model–format–platform combinations and executes their native Metal or CUDA paths.
summary_cn: 以模型、权重格式和平台的资格表限定支持范围，再提供原生 Zig 服务与专用执行。
motivation: Documented objective: serve qualified language-model checkpoints directly from a binary without a Python or MLX serving installation.
boundary: Owns loading, tokenization, serving and execution for admitted combinations; experimental Living Weights is a separate model-changing feature.
reuse: Reuses existing model checkpoints, quantization encodings and platform GPU runtimes; reading an MLX format does not mean running MLX.
tradeoff: Packed formats and backend capabilities constrain fusion; a supported model name alone does not qualify every checkpoint.
construction: Public artifacts show native Zig model paths and format-aware readers. The authoring workflow and division of implementation work are not disclosed.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; native code or compact packaging does not identify its authorship process.
cost: Development time, token/GPU expenditure and long-term engineering costs are not disclosed.
validation: The README provides qualification tables, golden-test commands and cache-state checks; this survey did not rerun them.
maintenance: Qualification is versioned and hardware-specific; adding readers or platforms creates additional compatibility obligations.

title: Halogen Flash: specialize a closed binary to one chip
summary: A distributed binary targets one Qwen family and AMD Strix Halo, with public deployment and quantization descriptions.
summary_cn: 以一个模型家族和一类芯片为边界发布专用二进制，公开部署与量化说明。
motivation: The README explicitly trades portability for model-and-chip specialization, targeting long local coding-agent sessions.
boundary: Public material exposes deployment and behavior; the core engine and complete tensor-level quantization choices are not publicly inspectable.
reuse: Uses pretrained weights and accepts selected llama.cpp GGUF files; underlying implementation reuse is not established by public documentation.
tradeoff: Mixed precision and narrow hardware support shape the result; repeatable binary benchmarks cannot substitute for source-level inspection.
construction: Documentation describes dedicated attention/expert kernels, separate state budgets and a paged n-gram lookup table.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; serving agents does not establish that agents built the engine.
cost: Development time, token usage and engineering costs are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: The publisher provides verification and benchmark modes; their numerical guarantees and performance were not independently reproduced here.
maintenance: Compatibility follows binary releases and supported hardware; maintenance effort and reproducible source builds are not established.

title: Magnitude: specialize kernels inside MLX execution
summary: The reviewed Metal path captures typed operations and constructs specialized fused kernels inside MLX’s execution machinery.
summary_cn: 在 MLX 执行体系内捕获带类型的运算，按数值契约与张量布局构造专用融合内核。
motivation: The README presents local, hardware-specific compilation and tuning for agent inference; historical framework bottlenecks are not established.
boundary: The inspected kernel layer owns planning and generated entry points, not a second device runtime or independent scheduler.
reuse: Retains MLX arrays, tracing, compilation and dependency management, combining upstream primitives with handwritten Metal implementations.
tradeoff: Encodings, shapes and numerical contracts restrict legal composition; unfamiliar operations and shapeless compilation retain upstream behavior.
construction: Capture operations, select compatible implementations, emit Metal entry points, then reconnect the transformed graph to native MLX compilation.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; an engine for agents is not automatically an agent-generated engine.
cost: Total development effort and amortization of device-specific tuning are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: Design documents define qualification obligations; inspecting compiler code does not prove every handwritten kernel satisfies them.
maintenance: The evidence covers inference-v2 Metal/MLX; other backends and continuing qualification costs remain outside this audit.

title: KTransformers: integrate CPU expert execution with GPU serving
summary: A specialized heterogeneous backend uses CPU capacity and instruction sets for MoE experts while retaining GPU serving components.
summary_cn: 将面向 CPU 指令集与 NUMA 的专家执行后端接入 GPU 服务路径。
motivation: The documented use case is large MoE inference with limited GPU resources and substantial CPU memory.
boundary: The reviewed kt-kernel path is an integrated backend; it is distinct from legacy injection examples and separate training features.
reuse: Reuses GPU serving integrations, model formats and libraries including a llamafile-based CPU backend, alongside AMX/AVX-specific implementations.
tradeoff: The useful partition depends on CPU ISA, NUMA placement, precision and communication costs; CPU capacity alone does not guarantee speed.
construction: The project documents kt-kernel implementations and serving integration. Its development iterations and division of work between people and tools are not established.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources. Supporting agent workloads does not disclose an AI development process.
cost: Hardware configurations are documented; controlled construction-time and maintenance-cost accounting is not disclosed.
validation: README support matrices and an AMX MoE implementation were inspected; benchmark and correctness claims were not independently reproduced.
maintenance: Kernel variants, weight formats and serving integrations evolve separately and require compatible versions.

title: Nunchaku: build execution around an SVDQuant artifact
summary: A low-bit diffusion backend co-designs packed weights and fused execution so the outlier-correction branch remains affordable.
summary_cn: 围绕 SVDQuant 权重与低秩修正分支，联合设计低比特布局和融合执行。
motivation: The documented problem is that an otherwise useful low-rank branch adds activation reads and writes that erode quantization gains.
boundary: Implements specialized diffusion-model execution components and integrations; it does not replace all text encoding, decoding or application layers.
reuse: Uses DeepCompressor-prepared checkpoints and existing PyTorch/Diffusers integrations; low-bit and low-rank CUDA kernels supply the specialized path.
tradeoff: Quantization changes numerical computation; reduced offloading, optional caching and checkpoint changes must be separated from kernel-level benefits.
construction: Source exposes custom CUDA operations through Python model adapters. The development chronology and division of automated and human work are not established.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; model quantization and automatic kernels do not imply coding-agent authorship.
cost: Calibration and conversion are preparation work; developer effort and total construction economics are not disclosed.
validation: Public examples, quality results and kernels support inspection, but this survey did not independently reproduce image quality or speed.
maintenance: Support depends on checkpoint format, model adapters and CUDA/PyTorch compatibility; maintenance effort is not quantified.

title: ExLlamaV3: couple low-bit artifacts to a dedicated library
summary: A local-inference library couples EXL3 encoding, quantized state and qualified execution paths for consumer GPUs.
summary_cn: 将 EXL3 编码、低比特状态与专用执行路径配套，服务消费级 GPU 本地推理。
motivation: The README targets flexible quantization, parallel inference and large models with limited consumer-GPU resources.
boundary: Provides model execution and generation machinery; the recommended OpenAI-compatible server is the separate TabbyAPI project.
reuse: EXL3 builds on QTIP; the project uses PyTorch and credits FlashAttention, Marlin and vendored Flash Linear Attention kernels.
tradeoff: Weight/KV precision, model layout and decode geometry constrain optimized paths; quantized results are not the full-precision reference.
construction: Public artifacts provide a dedicated inference library and conversion tools. The development workflow is not disclosed; weight conversion is deployment preparation, not engine authorship evidence.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources. Automated conversion and dispatch do not identify the software’s development process.
cost: The README reports conversion in minutes to hours on a high-end consumer GPU, depending on model size; total engineering costs are unknown.
validation: Optimization documentation and quantized-cache code were inspected; conversion quality and end-to-end speed were not independently reproduced.
maintenance: Model support, kernel eligibility and PyTorch/CUDA/Triton versions create separate compatibility obligations.

title: Mirage MPK: compile an explicit graph into persistent execution
summary: A compiler/runtime turns an assembled LLM task graph into persistent GPU execution spanning computation and communication.
summary_cn: 将显式组装的 LLM 任务图编译为覆盖计算与通信的持久 GPU 执行程序。
motivation: The documented objective is reducing inference latency by moving model-wide execution into a single persistent megakernel.
boundary: This case covers the MPK branch and its supported task graph, not automatic support for arbitrary Hugging Face models.
reuse: Attaches existing PyTorch tensors, uses CUDA and NVSHMEM resources, and assembles supported fused operations rather than inventing model weights.
tradeoff: Graph coverage, tensor geometry and worker/scheduler allocation constrain generated programs; hardware resources must be budgeted explicitly.
construction: Define inputs, outputs and fused tasks, configure GPU workers, compile the graph and execute the resulting persistent program.
ai_role: Not established in reviewed sources; compiler automation is not itself evidence of coding-agent participation.
cost: End-to-end construction, tuning and maintenance costs are not disclosed in reviewed sources.
validation: Public demos and profiling interfaces expose execution; this survey inspected compiler/runtime boundaries without reproducing reported speedups.
maintenance: New models require supported task implementations and graph assembly; hardware changes require configuration and compatibility checks.

title: Lily: one checkpoint, explicit compatibility boundary
summary: A narrowly qualified Rust/Metal engine exposes the compatibility decisions made when rebuilding model execution.
summary_cn: 为单一检查点重建 Rust/Metal 执行路径，并明确舍弃通用兼容性。
motivation: Reduce local execution overhead for a particular Qwen hybrid MoE workload on recent Apple GPUs.
boundary: Owns checkpoint validation, model graph, kernels, generation and a small session cache.
reuse: Reuses MLX-affine checkpoint storage, tokenizer dependencies and Metal; model execution does not use MLX.
tradeoff: Only the supported architecture and quantization layout; greedy text generation with a restricted API.
construction: Rust model paths dispatch Metal shaders compiled at runtime. Contributions require CPU-reference kernel tests and route-boundary checks.
ai_role: Not established by the inspected sources; runtime use by coding agents is not authorship evidence.
cost: Development hours, total cost and maintenance effort are not disclosed.
validation: Kernel, shader, API and golden-model tests are public. Checkpoint-backed tests can be skipped; author benchmark reports are not independent replication.
maintenance: Pinned toolchain and checkpoints bound regression work; another architecture requires implementation and renewed numerical qualification.

title: Lithos Metal: compiled mixer programs and GPU-resident control
summary: A standalone compiler/runtime turns selected model graphs into Apple-specific execution programs.
summary_cn: 把模型图、芯片配置和生成状态共同编译为 Apple 专用执行程序。
motivation: Avoid repeated dispatch and intermediate traffic while retaining enough GPU parallelism for local Qwen inference.
boundary: Owns typed IR, fusion, memory planning, kernel emission, program ABI and generation-state replay.
reuse: Uses Metal and checkpoint formats; Mirage inspires the task model but is not a runtime dependency.
tradeoff: Fusion is layer-local and recipe-dependent. Normalization fusion may alter rounding; unmeasured chips use conservative fallbacks.
construction: Model packages lower into registered operations; chip recipes select layouts and task schedules before native pipeline compilation. Extension contracts specify qualification gates.
ai_role: Not established by the inspected sources; runtime use by coding agents is not authorship evidence.
cost: Development hours, total cost and maintenance effort are not disclosed.
validation: Contract, kernel, layer and model-oracle tiers exist. Published target-compute projections must not be read as end-to-end throughput.
maintenance: New models and devices need adapter/recipe qualification; the documented extension workflow does not quantify long-term maintenance effort.

title: Saragossa: resident decode with explicit state ownership
summary: A Rust/Metal engine concentrates on local latency and controlled model-state lifetimes.
summary_cn: 用 Rust/Metal 原生模型路径管理驻留状态，面向本地低延迟推理。
motivation: Reduce per-operation synchronization for resident local decode, including selected text and speech workloads.
boundary: Owns model forward paths, Metal dispatch, KV/recurrent state, scratch lifetimes and prefix snapshots.
reuse: Loads MLX-affine weights; speech golden fixtures were captured from a frozen earlier MLX-based reference.
tradeoff: Local single-user policies, supported quantization layouts and precision switches constrain the comparison scope.
construction: Source separates resident-state ownership from kernel implementation. Leased scratch buffers prevent overlapping live intermediates from silently aliasing.
ai_role: A source comment attributes a non-clonable GPU-state constraint to Codex D; the review process, coding role and overall AI contribution are not established.
cost: Development hours, total cost and maintenance effort are not disclosed.
validation: Golden fixtures, differential tests and author benchmarks are exposed. Near-tie drift and precision settings need inspection; no model run was performed.
maintenance: Runtime switches and golden provenance support regression diagnosis; broader hardware qualification and lifecycle cost are unknown.

title: TurboFieldfare: a runtime designed around an 8 GB memory budget
summary: A Gemma-specific Swift/Metal runtime makes storage and execution policy part of the same design.
summary_cn: 围绕 8 GB 内存限制联合重建 Gemma 的专家存储、调度和执行路径。
motivation: Run a checkpoint larger than available memory while keeping common weights and working state bounded.
boundary: Owns expert packaging, installation, residency, prefill/decode scheduling and model-specific kernels.
reuse: Reuses swift-transformers tokenization; Transformers, MLX and GGML implementations provide numerical and kernel references.
tradeoff: Narrow model support and SSD-dependent latency replace broad compatibility and fully resident speed.
construction: Published experiments trace the move from demand paging to explicit reads, cache policy changes, kernel designs and later reversals.
ai_role: AI participation in the construction is not established by the inspected sources.
cost: The curated inventory records 103 experiments, not total developer time or monetary cost.
validation: The project reports end-to-end and quality gates, including rejected low-bit KV paths. The inventory is curated design history, not independent replication.
maintenance: Model-free tests and real-model acceptance are separated; the effort to sustain future models and platform changes is unknown.

title: TUFF: extending a streaming runtime across model families
summary: A substantive TurboFieldfare fork retains bounded streaming while adding model-specific execution paths.
summary_cn: 从 TurboFieldfare 深度分叉，保留有界专家流式机制并扩展模型执行路径。
motivation: Make selected large MoE checkpoints usable on ordinary memory-constrained Macs.
boundary: Owns native model execution, expert I/O, memory policy and the model-owning decode service.
reuse: Explicitly credits TurboFieldfare for the original Gemma runtime and streaming foundation; uses Swift/Metal and tokenizer packages.
tradeoff: Each new architecture needs format, kernel, prompt and real-run qualification; hardware results remain configuration-specific.
construction: Extends TurboFieldfare with Gated DeltaNet state updates, fused projections and Qwen gated-attention paths. Qualification calls for CPU references, toy-forward tests, prompt goldens and a real model run.
ai_role: The maintainer explicitly discloses using AI on TUFF and requires human line-by-line review; task division and amount are unspecified.
cost: Development hours, total cost and maintenance effort are not disclosed.
validation: Public model-free checks and author/community benchmarks exist; most direct release testing is on one 16 GB M2 machine.
maintenance: The contribution guide preserves old model formats and release recovery; the cost of the expanded compatibility surface is unquantified.

title: Colibri: separate C engines with shared streaming components
summary: A collection of architecture-specific C engines treats expert residency and model execution as explicit design responsibilities.
summary_cn: 按模型族实现独立 C 执行器，共享专家流式与可选设备后端。
motivation: Execute very large sparse models without requiring all expert weights to remain in RAM.
boundary: Owns per-family forward paths, container readers, routed expert stores and optional device tiers.
reuse: Uses native OS I/O and optional GPU APIs; provenance notes identify adapted DwarfStar and Swiftlet components.
tradeoff: Supported formats and backend coverage differ by engine; storage capacity gains do not imply fast interactive generation.
construction: Independent model-family programs are checked against generated references. Contribution rules preserve a working default CPU route and require targeted validation.
ai_role: Inspected porting notes contain agent-oriented plans, but do not establish the actual division of coding work.
cost: Development hours, total cost and maintenance effort are not disclosed.
validation: Strict synthetic oracles include an explicit teacher-forcing mismatch allowance and exact greedy checks. They are narrower than full-model quality validation.
maintenance: The project keeps an engine/backend matrix and targeted tests; maintenance cost across this matrix has not been disclosed.

title: ane.cpp: hardware probes feed an ANE execution stack
summary: An ANE-LM fork uses empirical hardware probes to guide runtime fusion, chunking and dispatch changes.
summary_cn: 将 ANE 探针实验的结果落实为融合、分块与调度修改。
motivation: Explore useful ANE offload for background and shared-process inference, not only peak foreground token rate.
boundary: Owns MIL kernel construction, private API invocation, persistent compilation caches and CPU/ANE dispatch boundaries.
reuse: Forks ANE-LM; reuses CPU operations and reverse-engineering findings from the companion field guide.
tradeoff: Selected dense text models only; private APIs, numerical constraints and CPU fallback limit portability.
construction: The documented workflow first tests isolated operations against CPU references, then ports surviving findings into the model runtime and measures changes.

cost: Total construction and maintenance effort is unknown; training and inference performance metrics cannot substitute for those measurements.

title: SEIS: sustained evolution of an existing inference engine
summary: A fixed coding agent repeatedly changes a working engine, carrying implementation and reports between sessions. This is a whole-stack construction and validation case, not inclusion of a teaching engine merely because it is small.
summary_cn: 固定编程 Agent，通过继承代码与报告持续重构已有引擎，涉及内核、运行时和解码；收录的是构建与验证过程，不是因为 mini-sglang 代码少。论文实验与公开十轮示例分开记录。
motivation: Study whether accumulated agent work can improve an entire inference system rather than isolated kernels or independent one-shot attempts.
boundary: Starts from mini-sglang, not an empty implementation. The inspected trial-10 engine installs quantized weights and uses graph-captured greedy selection; the paper additionally describes prompt-lookup verification and coordinated KV/runtime changes.
reuse: Retains mini-sglang infrastructure, pretrained checkpoints, PyTorch/CUDA and existing attention facilities where used. The coding agent itself is not trained or evolved.
tradeoff: The principal paper setting is a small model, one H100 and single-request greedy inference. Low-bit execution is not the original numerical computation; results are not a general multi-model or concurrent-serving comparison.
construction: Paper: independent sessions, sequential inheritance and synchronized chains. Public scaffold: a shell loop launches ten fresh coding sessions and keeps their logs; written instructions and learning notes guide subsequent work. These are related but distinct levels of disclosed implementation.
ai_role: Agent participation is explicit in the paper and executable session driver. Initial goals and evaluation rules are human-provided; researchers revise evaluation after discovering untested failure modes.
cost: The public demo reports approximately USD 100 of Claude usage for ten trials. The inspected driver sets a USD 20 per-trial cap, not measured spend. These values do not account for the paper experiment, human work, GPU costs or lifetime maintenance.
validation: The paper checks numerical drift and downstream math/retrieval performance, and reports previously accepted candidates with vocabulary, termination or state-handling failures. Its best-engine audit is distinct from those failed candidates. The public driver and inspected evolved code do not by themselves reproduce the full paper evaluation.
maintenance: Code and reports are inherited, and working ideas may transfer between chains. Misleading reports and integration repairs remain part of the process; long-term production adaptation costs are not established.

title: VibeServe / VibeSys: generation-time serving specialization
summary: Connects generation-time model/hardware/workload specialization to a concrete serving-system initiative; the broader generator and its scenario-specific outputs are distinct artifacts.
summary_cn: 按模型、硬件和负载构建专用服务栈；区分 VibeServe 论文中的产物与现行 VibeSys 通用构建框架，非推理任务不在本条范围。

boundary: The artifact is a construction framework whose VibeServe initiative produces target-specific serving stacks. It is not itself one universal inference runtime.
reuse: The documented workflow reuses serving knowledge, profiling tools, coding agents and existing model/kernel facilities where appropriate; generated outputs must disclose their own dependencies.
tradeoff: Each candidate is qualified against its scenario and evaluation contract. The broad current framework also includes non-inference tasks; that breadth is not inferred coverage of generated serving systems.
construction: The paper separates outer design search and inner implementation/evaluation. The inspected current code stores evaluator, workload and environment identities with an evaluation recipe, and rejects parallel candidate modes without suitable isolation.
ai_role: Coding agents participate explicitly. Humans supply objectives, domain knowledge and evaluation definitions; current framework-side measurement is distinct from an agent claiming a pass.
cost: This review does not establish a comparable lifecycle cost. Any reported campaign budget must be attached to its paper scenario and separated from validation, integration and subsequent maintenance.
validation: Inspected the README and host evaluation wiring, alongside the paper and lab report. Contract-specific tests and a read-only reviewer are not universal numerical or service-correctness proofs. No campaign was reproduced.
maintenance: The project now uses the VibeSys name and a broader task framework. Pin current code separately from the VibeServe paper rather than transferring historical results to all later versions.

title: AutoMegaKernel: checked generation of model-level execution
summary: A model-program construction case combining a restricted agent edit surface, deterministic lowering and schedule checks; contrasts with unconstrained whole-runtime generation.
summary_cn: 通过受限调度 IR、模型降低和静态检查生成整步执行程序；不是完整服务引擎，也不是所有代码都可自由改写的 Agent 构建。
motivation: Reduce per-operator execution boundaries while making generated whole-model schedules inspectable before device launch.
boundary: One persistent cooperative launch executes one forward pass; counters reset between launches, KV persists and the host advances decoding. Instruction tuning and ScheduleConfig search are different edit surfaces.
reuse: A handwritten trusted VM, instruction ABI, model importer, CUDA runtime and reference implementations remain shared. No per-model handwritten CUDA does not mean the trusted base is automatically generated.
tradeoff: Current inference scope is restricted to supported model graphs and hardware. Paper shape-level performance and real-checkpoint quality results are separate; low-bit comparisons are not equal-precision controls.
construction: The documented first loop tunes an ABI micro-kernel; the second proposes structured schedules lowered by the fixed VM. The inspected IR checks counters, dependencies, placement and buffer ordering.
ai_role: The compiler exposes an explicit coding-agent harness. Structured schedule search must not be described as unrestricted synthesis of a new runtime.
cost: Unattended self-tuning demonstrations compare against their own starting point. This inspection establishes neither full construction cost nor maintenance savings over a shared serving framework.
validation: Inspected schedule/ir.py, including static dependency and hazard checks. Some hazard checks are task-count-capped; references and supported VM semantics remain trusted. This is not a mechanized proof and no CUDA tests were run here.
maintenance: New operators, model features or device targets require compatible importer, ABI, validator and VM support; broad self-retargeting claims do not remove these obligations.

title: Cloudflare Infire: platform-specific serving reconstruction
summary: An industrial platform-specialization case documenting why a provider rebuilt execution instead of only configuring a general framework; useful without an AI-development attribution.
summary_cn: 围绕边缘节点的 CPU、启动和隔离约束重建 Rust 服务执行栈；采用官方工程披露，明确核心专有，并区分初始实现与后续多 GPU 扩展。
motivation: Cloudflare describes a mismatch between its geographically distributed resource-constrained nodes and the deployment assumptions of its earlier vLLM setup.
boundary: The disclosed stack includes the HTTP server, batcher and model executor, with model-specific kernels and execution graphs. Later work extends parallel model execution.
reuse: The report names Hyper, HuggingFace tokenizers, CUDA and cuBLASLt for suitable operations. A native replacement still retains shared libraries and established batching/cache mechanisms.
tradeoff: Specialization is to a provider platform and its deployment envelope, not one checkpoint. Proprietary implementation prevents independent source-level checking in this review.
construction: The original report describes a Rust rewrite with asynchronous loading, JIT compilation and hardware-focused kernels. The later report describes added multi-GPU and memory/startup work.
ai_role: No direct AI-construction attribution was established from the reviewed engineering reports. Do not infer it from the project being a newly built engine.
cost: The initial report measures CPU usage and throughput in selected deployment configurations; those operational observations are not a measurement of development or lifecycle cost.
validation: Two official engineering reports were reviewed. The initial comparison distinguishes bare-metal vLLM, sandboxed vLLM and CPU-constrained operation; keep those conditions separate. No engine execution or source audit was possible from these materials.
maintenance: The later multi-GPU report supplies concrete evolution evidence. Record new scope as a later stage rather than rewriting the original report or assuming all future model support.

title: Kog Inference Engine: model and device co-designed execution
summary: An industrial model/runtime/hardware co-design case with an explicitly narrow low-latency operating point; distinguishes a purpose-built execution architecture from a generic serving configuration.
summary_cn: 按单请求低延迟目标联动设计模型、持久执行与多卡通信；依据厂商文档，明确 Laneformer/DTP、八卡和 FP16 条件，不当作原模型通用加速结果。
motivation: Target the low-latency single-request regime rather than maximizing aggregate throughput through large batches.
boundary: The vendor describes a monokernel managing sequence generation, sampling, state and cross-device communication, not only an isolated matrix multiplication.
reuse: Pretrained model assets, AMD/NVIDIA devices and their programming/runtime interfaces remain prerequisites. The vendor claims its own execution implementation; public engine source was not established.
tradeoff: The reviewed preview combines a roughly 2B FP16 Laneformer model with eight GPUs and batch one. Delayed tensor parallelism changes the model architecture, so runtime and model contributions must be separated.
construction: The engineering report describes compile-time work assignment, device-side synchronization, continuous weight streaming and delayed cross-device reductions. These are documentation-backed design claims, not inspected implementation paths.
ai_role: No direct coding-agent construction evidence was established in the reviewed materials; relevance comes from execution co-design.
cost: Reported latency and tokens per second do not quantify GPU cost per request, utilization under mixed load, construction effort or lifetime maintenance.
validation: Reviewed the technical monokernel article and matching preview conditions. Neither is an independent replication or a complete quality-equivalence protocol; announced future model support remains a roadmap.
maintenance: Model and device co-design creates adaptation obligations. The release of model weights, where applicable, must not be confused with publication of the inference engine implementation.
